01.actor: Anan bar Hiyya of Hagra / the Sages investigating a found bill of divorce
01.event: A bill of divorce was found in Sura in the name of Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a, and the Sages searched the whole region and found only one man of that name.
01.turn: Witnesses testified that on the day the document was written, that Anan bar Hiyya was with them in Neharde'a, not in Sura.
01.outcome: The case ends in a legal disagreement: Abaye says there is no concern, Rava says he might have travelled miraculously fast or given instructions remotely; no ruling on the woman is narrated.
01.summary: A divorce document was found in Sura, signed in the name of Anan bar Hiyya of Neharde'a. The Sages searched from Sura to Neharde'a and found only one man by that name, Anan bar Hiyya of Hagra. But witnesses came and said that on the day the document was written he had been with them in Neharde'a. Abaye and Rava then argued over whether the document could still be his.
01.missing: What actually happened to the document and the woman; the passage turns into a legal debate rather than an ending.

02.actor: A debtor who hid his money behind a gentile
02.event: A debtor claimed his money belonged to a gentile so his creditor could not collect it.
02.turn: Because he acted improperly, the Sages acted improperly with him.
02.outcome: The Sages forced him to sell his land himself and pay the creditor.
02.summary: Rav Pappa asked Rav Hama about a ruling attributed to Rava, that a debtor can be made to sell his land himself to pay a creditor. Rav Hama explained the real incident behind it: the debtor had pretended his money belonged to a gentile to avoid paying. Because he behaved dishonestly, the Sages dealt harshly with him and made him sell the land.
02.missing: The incident is only summarized in a sentence; no details of who, when, or how it was carried out.

03.actor: The son of Nehunya the well digger
03.event: Despite his father's merit in digging wells for the public, Nehunya's son died of thirst.
03.turn: His father's merit did not protect him, which Rabbi Abba explains as God being exacting to a hair's breadth with the righteous.
03.summary: Nehunya dug wells for travellers, and when his daughter fell into a cistern she was saved, as Rabbi Hanina ben Dosa had foreseen. Yet Rabbi Abba reports that even so Nehunya's son died of thirst. He explains this with verses teaching that God is extremely exacting with those closest to Him.
03.missing: The story of the son's death itself is only stated, not narrated; how or why he died is not told.

04.event: An uncircumcised priest sprinkled the purification waters.
04.outcome: The Sages ruled his sprinkling valid.
04.summary: A baraita reports an incident in which an uncircumcised man sprinkled the waters of purification, and the Sages declared his sprinkling valid.
04.missing: Who the man was, why he was uncircumcised, and any circumstances; the incident is a one-line precedent.

05.event: Funerals had become so expensive that families abandoned their dead and fled.
05.turn: Rabban Gamliel instructed that he himself be buried in plain linen.
05.outcome: Everyone followed his example, and the custom of simple burial garments took hold, down to Rav Pappa's day.
05.summary: Funerals once cost so much that relatives found the burial harder than the death and would sometimes leave the body and run away. Rabban Gamliel set an example by asking to be buried in simple linen. Everyone followed him, and by Rav Pappa's time people were buried even in cheap rough cloth.

06.actor: A man captured with his mother
06.event: A man, speaking casually, said that when he and his mother were held captive among gentiles he never stopped watching over her.
06.turn: Though a son cannot normally testify for his mother, his remark was an unconsidered aside.
06.outcome: Rabbi permitted the mother to marry a priest on the strength of his words.
06.summary: A man chatting offhandedly mentioned that he and his mother had been taken captive, and that whether he went to draw water or gather wood, his mind was always on her. The case came before Rabbi (or Rabbi Yehoshua ben Levi). Because the remark was casual and not formal testimony, Rabbi relied on it and allowed the mother to marry a priest.

07.event: Rav Kahana held beer belonging to the orphan Rav Mesharshiyya bar Hilkai and put off selling it until the Festival.
07.turn: He reasoned that even if it soured slightly, it would fetch ready cash at the Festival.
07.summary: Rav Kahana was looking after beer owned by an orphan, Rav Mesharshiyya bar Hilkai. Instead of selling it at once, he waited for the Festival, explaining that even if it spoiled a bit, it would sell then for good cash.
07.missing: Whether the plan worked or how the sale turned out.

08.actor: Residents of a crooked alleyway in Sura
08.event: Residents of an L-shaped alleyway in Sura set a rolled-up mat at its bend as a side post so they could carry on Shabbat.
08.turn: Rav Hisda said the arrangement matched neither Rav nor Shmuel.
08.outcome: The mat was declared ineffective, since the wind could blow it over.
08.summary: In Sura there was an L-shaped alleyway where people placed a rolled mat at the corner to allow carrying on Shabbat. Rav Hisda ruled it worthless under either Rav's or Shmuel's view, because a loose mat that the wind can knock down is not a real side post.
08.missing: Little action beyond the ruling; what the residents did afterward is not told.

09.actor: Rav Pappa and Yehuda bar Mareimar
09.event: Rav Pappa went to write the marriage contract for his son's bride, and Yehuda bar Mareimar came out to honor him.
09.turn: At the door of the bride's house Yehuda tried to take his leave, and Rav Pappa saw he was unwilling to enter and asked why.
09.summary: Rav Pappa arranged for his son to marry into the family of Abba of Sura and went to oversee the writing of the marriage contract. Yehuda bar Mareimar came out to greet him, but at the door he tried to leave. Rav Pappa invited him in and, seeing his reluctance, asked whether it was because of Shmuel's teaching against taking part in transferring an inheritance.
09.missing: Yehuda's answer and whether he went in; the ending lies beyond the segments shown.

10.actor: The Sages, Rav, and the messengers
10.event: Faced with the Shmuel-Karna dispute about a minor betrothed without her father's consent, the Sages sent the question to Rav with the names of the two opinions swapped.
10.turn: Rav, thinking Shmuel held the opposite view, swore by God that she needs both a bill of divorce and refusal.
10.outcome: Rav declared that Shmuel would never say otherwise, unknowingly endorsing Shmuel's real opinion.
10.summary: Shmuel ruled that a minor betrothed without her father's consent needs both a divorce and refusal, and Karna found this contradictory. The Sages sent the question to Rav but reversed whose opinion was whose. Rav swore that she needs both, and said heaven forbid Shmuel should say anything else, thereby backing Shmuel without knowing it.
10.missing: Why the names were reversed and how Rav's answer was received.

11.actor: A man who made a conditional divorce
11.event: A man gave a bill of divorce that would take effect if he did not return within thirty days.
11.turn: He came back just in time but the ferry was on the far side, so he stood at the river shouting 'See that I came!'
11.outcome: Shmuel ruled that this did not count as returning, so the divorce took effect.
11.summary: A man handed over a bill of divorce on condition that it would be valid if he did not come back within thirty days. At the end of the thirty days he reached the river, but the ferry was on the other side and he could not cross. He called out to people across the water that he had come, but Shmuel ruled that this was not a return.

13.actor: A man from Eretz Yisrael and Rabbi Hanina
13.event: A man whose brother died childless in Bei Hoza'a asked Rabbi Hanina whether he could go down to Babylonia to perform levirate marriage.
13.turn: Rabbi Hanina said the brother had left the Land to marry a 'Samaritan' and God had rightly killed him.
13.outcome: Rabbi Hanina told him not to follow his brother out of the Land.
13.summary: A man's brother had died childless, leaving a widow in far-off Bei Hoza'a in Babylonia. He asked Rabbi Hanina whether he should go there to marry her. Rabbi Hanina answered harshly that the brother had left the Land of Israel to marry a foreign woman, blessed be God who killed him, and asked whether this man wanted to follow him down.

14.actor: A millstone owner and his renter
14.event: A man rented his millstone to another in exchange for grinding services.
14.turn: The owner got rich, bought his own millstone and donkey, and demanded money instead of grinding.
14.summary: A man rented out his millstone, and the renter paid by grinding the owner's grain. Later the owner grew rich, bought a millstone and donkey of his own, and demanded rent in money. The renter refused, saying he had only agreed to grind.
14.missing: The ruling or how the dispute ended; only Ravina's initial legal reasoning follows.

15.event: A dying man said, 'My property goes to Toviya,' and after his death a man named Toviya came to claim it.
15.turn: There was doubt whether this was the Toviya he meant.
15.outcome: Rabbi Yohanan ruled 'Toviya has come,' and gave him the property.
15.summary: A man on his deathbed said his property should go to Toviya. When he died, a Toviya came forward. Rabbi Yohanan ruled that the Toviya who came should get it, without worrying that a different Toviya was meant.

16.actor: Mar Zutra and a rebellious wife
16.event: A wife said she was disgusted with her husband, and Mar Zutra compelled her to stay with him.
16.turn: From that couple came Rabbi Hanina of Sura.
16.outcome: The Gemara says the good result was heavenly help and not a precedent.
16.summary: A woman refused her husband, saying he disgusted her, and Mar Zutra forced her to remain married. The couple later had a son, the sage Rabbi Hanina of Sura. The Gemara cautions that this good outcome came from divine help and should not justify such coercion.

17.actor: Rav Pappa and Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda
17.event: At his son Abba Mar's wedding, Rav Pappa poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak, who did not stand for him.
17.summary: Rav Pappa was serving drinks at his son Abba Mar's wedding. When he poured a cup for Rav Yitzhak son of Rav Yehuda, Rav Yitzhak did not rise before him, and Rav Pappa was offended.
17.missing: Any response or resolution; the anecdote is cited only to make a legal point.

18.event: Ravnai came to sell sesame and reported Shmuel's ruling that a witness and judge may combine.
18.turn: Ameimar praised the ruling, and Rav Ashi retorted that he praised it only because his grandfather had, and that Rava had already refuted it.
18.outcome: The ruling was rejected as refuted.
18.summary: Ravnai, brother of Rabbi Hiyya bar Abba, came to sell sesame and quoted Shmuel's view that a witness and a judge can join together. Ameimar called it an excellent ruling. Rav Ashi mocked him for praising it just because his mother's father had, pointing out that Rava had already disproved it.
18.missing: The exchange is mostly an argument over a ruling; little happens beyond the rebuke.

19.event: Rabbi Yohanan's relatives, burdened with their stepmother's daily medical costs, asked his advice.
19.turn: He told them to fix a lump sum with the doctor, so the cost would come out of her marriage settlement.
19.outcome: He later regretted it, saying he had acted like a legal advisor, since an important person must not favor his relatives.
19.summary: Rabbi Yohanan's relatives had to pay for their father's widow, who needed treatment every day. He advised them to agree a fixed fee with the doctor, which would shift the cost onto her marriage settlement. Afterward he regretted it, saying he had made himself like a lawyer coaching a party, which a man of his standing should not do.

20.actor: Rav Aha bar Ya'akov and Rava
20.event: Rav Aha bar Ya'akov allowed the freed sons of the maidservant Yudan to marry each other's former wives.
20.turn: Rava challenged him that Rav Sheshet had forbidden it.
20.outcome: Rav Aha replied that Rav Sheshet forbade it and he permitted it.
20.summary: The sons of a maidservant named Yudan were freed, and Rav Aha bar Ya'akov permitted them to marry one another's wives. Rava objected that Rav Sheshet had prohibited this. Rav Aha answered simply that Rav Sheshet forbade it and he himself allowed it.
20.missing: Whether the marriages took place; the incident is essentially a ruling and its challenge.
